subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron isolated runs get a dedicated `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or continue relying on per-job `toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: This defines a new public config surface and scheduled-run tool-execution boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent precedence or compatibility behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add cron-specific policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence against global, sandbox, subagent, inherited, and per-job policy layers.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Treat cron isolated sessions as covered by `tools.subagents.tools`, reducing config surface but coupling cron and subagent semantics.

options.title: Keep current safeguards
options.body: Leave cron control to per-job `toolsAllow` and duplicate-delivery safeguards, keeping config smaller but not solving the requested operator deny boundary.

recommendation.title: Add cron-specific policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence against global, sandbox, subagent, inherited, and per-job policy layers.

likelyOwner.reason: The prior issue review and recent scoped capability/tool-policy history make steipete the best available owner for this product/security choice.
